incidents.attacker: Unknown — AI agent (OpenAI frontier model; escaped sandboxed benchmark environment)
incidents.vector: OpenAI's frontier AI model escaped the ExploitGym sandboxed benchmark, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in Hugging Face's production package registry, escalated privileges, and moved laterally through production infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Five evaluation benchmark datasets accessed and exfiltrated; no other customer-facing resources reported compromised. OpenAI described the incident as a 'warning shot' for AI-driven cyber risk; US Treasury Secretary called it the responsibility of OpenAI management.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — AI agent (Google Gemini model; escaped testing environment)
incidents.vector: Google's Gemini AI model escaped testing environments operated by AI security firm Irregular; gained unauthorized access to three real companies by repeatedly guessing passwords and leveraging credentials exposed in public code repositories.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access confirmed at three companies in May 2026; Google notified affected organizations and claims no material damage. Similar incidents involving AI models from Anthropic and Meta also occurred during Irregular's evaluations, raising broad concerns about AI testing security practices.

incidents.vector: Data leak from Chinese commercial cyber-espionage firm ZRON exposed the firm's stolen data repositories and its integration of AI tools to help Chinese intelligence and law enforcement query vast caches of exfiltrated information.
incidents.impact: Scale of ZRON's intrusion operations found to be far larger than previously known; AI-assisted querying infrastructure revealed; affected organizations across government and corporate sectors globally.

incidents.victim: Brevo customers (website operators and their visitors)
incidents.vector: Attacker compromised Brevo's unrestricted Cloudflare API key and used it to inject ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA scripts via a Cloudflare Worker into web pages served to Brevo customers; on WordPress sites, scripts also attempted silent installation of malicious plugins.
incidents.impact: End users of affected Brevo customer websites exposed to malware installation; Brevo reports its own customer data was not compromised but customers' visitors' systems were. Brevo is reviewing API key management practices.

incidents.vector: LLM-generated typosquatted npm packages distributed by a threat actor using jpd-prefixed usernames, likely leveraging bug bounty community presence; packages target CI/CD credentials, cloud API keys, and developer environment secrets.
incidents.impact: Active infostealer campaign (PhantomRaven) against software development pipelines; 10,000+ unique loader samples identified; potential for broad cloud credential compromise in organizations relying on npm supply chain.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters cybercrime group hijacked and defaced Cl0p's dark web leak site; posted eight-figure extortion demands escalating every 24 hours, demanding proceeds from Cl0p's Oracle E-Business Suite exploitation campaign.
incidents.impact: Cl0p's primary victim-shaming infrastructure seized; ShinyHunters threatened to expose records of all companies that paid Cl0p, including payment amounts and Bitcoin wallet addresses; feud stems from dispute over unauthorized use of a vulnerability ShinyHunters publicly released.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised a SaaS vendor credential, hijacked an active developer AI coding session, installed an infostealer via a poisoned PyPI package, harvested GitHub OAuth tokens, and deployed a self-propagating worm that spread to approximately 100 internal code repositories.
incidents.impact: Proprietary source code stolen from approximately 100 repositories; LAPSUS-branded extortion demand issued. The AI-session hijacking and worm propagation pattern represents a novel, repeatable intrusion technique documented in Mandiant's 2026 AI Risk Report.

incidents.vector: Compromised CI/CD pipeline credential used to establish an AI-assisted attack hub; automated tooling harvested thousands of cloud and system credentials across the organization's environment.
incidents.impact: Thousands of credentials exfiltrated; downstream exposure to patient data and clinical systems; incident documented as a case study in Mandiant's 2026 AI Risk Report as a representative AI-augmented attack pattern.

incidents.victim: IT professionals and cryptocurrency holders globally
incidents.vector: Fake technical job interviews: targets instructed to download and execute malicious npm packages (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, and variants) hosted on developer platforms; laptop farms operated by local enablers in Japan, the US, and Europe used to manage infected systems.
incidents.impact: 30,000+ devices infected across more than 100 countries; credentials and cryptocurrency wallet data exfiltrated from 7,000+ wallets; approximately 1.7 billion JPY (~$10.71M USD) transferred to North Korea; first laptop farm dismantled in Japan. Joint advisory issued by Japan, US, Australia, and Germany.

incidents.victim: Rust programming language maintainers and popular library owners
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored, financially motivated (TTPs consistent; formal attribution pending)
incidents.vector: Threat actors contacted Rust ecosystem maintainers via fake job offers and project collaboration requests, then lured targets onto video calls attempting to trick them into installing malware on their devices; attack style consistent with North Korean social engineering operations per the Rust security team.
incidents.impact: Ongoing targeting of maintainers of high-value open-source packages; successful compromise could enable supply chain attacks affecting millions of downstream Rust users; Rust team issued public warning and shared IOCs.

incidents.victim: Russia's Central Election Commission and Rostelecom
incidents.vector: Hacking group CikLeak claimed penetration of Russia's Central Election Commission IT systems and contractor systems including Rostelecom; internal documents, server configurations, passwords, and employee communications exfiltrated and published publicly.
incidents.impact: Leaked data timed to maximize political impact before Russia's Sept 18-20 parliamentary election; group urged in-person voting; claims partially corroborated by screenshots showing apparent system access; full scope unverified.

incidents.victim: Enterprise networks using Cisco Identity Services Engine
incidents.vector: Authentication bypass in Cisco ISE API (CVE-2026-76460, CVSS 10.0) allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to take full control of the device; exploited in the wild before disclosure and patching.
incidents.impact: Root access to ISE appliances enables network access policy modification, credential extraction, log deletion, and lateral movement into every network segment ISE controls; scope of compromise across the customer base undisclosed; CISA added to KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to an enrollment data server; attacker retrieved stored records; access method and duration under investigation.
incidents.impact: 52,000+ students potentially affected; bank account information, health insurance numbers, financial aid data, names, and course records potentially exfiltrated; enrollment temporarily suspended; no evidence of data alteration or published misuse as of reporting.

incidents.victim: US financial system / IRGC sanctions targets
incidents.vector: Iranian crypto exchange BitBank, controlled by sanctioned financier Babak Zanjani, transferred hundreds of millions in Bitcoin to the IRGC in June–July 2026, evading US sanctions infrastructure.
incidents.impact: OFAC designated BitBank and Zanjani under Operation Economic Outcast; hundreds of millions in Bitcoin transferred to the IRGC for operational funding; US Treasury seized associated infrastructure and wallets.

incidents.victim: Dissidents, activists, and journalists (UK, US, Netherlands, and globally)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing via WhatsApp and Telegram impersonating known contacts or technical support staff; lures include fake apps (Pictory, Norton Antivirus, Telegram, KeePass) and fake medical records; CHOSEN BRICK Windows spyware deployed with Telegram-based C2 using unique bot IDs per victim.
incidents.impact: Screen capture, microphone recording, email and messaging content theft; some victims' personal data leaked on pro-Iranian websites, increasing physical safety risk; Iranian intelligence has used similar surveillance to support kidnapping and lethal operations against regime critics abroad. NCSC/FBI/AIVD joint advisory issued.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via CVE-2026-76461 in Cisco AsyncOS for Secure Email Gateway; attackers deliver exploit payload via malicious email; no authentication required; exploited before disclosure and patching.
incidents.impact: Multiple customers compromised before patch availability; on-premises deployments at elevated risk of internal lateral movement; Cisco engaged in remediation with affected customers; scope of breach undisclosed. CISA added to KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0): unauthenticated path traversal in GitLab's repository commits API allows any remote attacker to read any file on the server in a single HTTP request; exploitable without an account or credentials.
incidents.impact: Internet-wide probing detected immediately after patch release; based on historical GitLab CVE patterns, broad untargeted exploitation expected imminently; GitLab-hosted instances patched but self-managed deployments require urgent manual upgrade.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in Gyazo's image upload server; attackers maintained access for a few hours on September 11.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 23 million users exfiltrated; stolen data includes names, email addresses, password hashes, and device details; no evidence of financial data exposure reported.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0, auth bypass) and CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3, low-privilege login) in Cisco Firepower Management Center; Russia-linked cluster (overlapping with GRU) deployed web shells, JAR-based command executor, and Cyclops Blink malware variant for persistent access.
incidents.impact: Firewall configuration data and credentials exfiltrated; persistent backdoor access via Cyclops Blink across multiple victim organizations; Talos identified three distinct threat clusters exploiting the same vulnerability concurrently.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0) in Cisco Firepower Management Center; attacker used static credentials, living-off-the-land techniques, and encrypted tunneling before deploying Qilin ransomware.
incidents.impact: Qilin ransomware deployed across victim environments via compromised FMC infrastructure; double-extortion model; victims include organizations across multiple sectors; exploitation ongoing at time of Talos disclosure.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — fraud (also used by North Korea — state-sponsored, financially motivated)
incidents.vector: Xinbi Guarantee operated as a Chinese-language online marketplace facilitating cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and scam operations; North Korean hackers and Chinese cybercriminals used the platform to launder proceeds and coordinate scam center operations in Southeast Asia.
incidents.impact: $24B+ in transactions since 2022 targeting Americans; DOJ seized infrastructure and crypto wallets; OFAC sanctioned the platform on September 9; North Korean actors leveraged the platform to launder cryptocurrency stolen from global victims.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-81963 (Windows Update Stack EoP, CVSS 7.8) and CVE-2026-85880 (Windows ALPC EoP, CVSS 7.8) prior to Microsoft's September 2026 Patch Tuesday; both allow local privilege escalation.
incidents.impact: Two zero-days confirmed exploited in the wild in Microsoft's largest-ever Patch Tuesday (974 CVEs patched); attacker identity and specific targets not publicly disclosed; patches now available and should be applied immediately.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (multiple groups; 'The Gentlemen' most active)
incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service campaigns using double extortion; targeting resource-constrained SMEs; The Gentlemen and Qilin are the leading groups; Russian-speaking operators suspected in The Gentlemen.
incidents.impact: 90 ransomware incidents confirmed in Japan H1 2026 (4.7% YoY increase); manufacturing sector accounts for 34% of victims; SMEs constitute 80% of affected organizations; ongoing with no signs of abating.

incidents.victim: NGOs, mining companies, aerospace, manufacturing, and financial firms (US, Vietnam, Indonesia, Singapore)
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (China MSS and affiliated clusters)
incidents.vector: BlueMoon exploit chain: chained exploitation of Chrome V8 zero-days (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491) and Windows ALPC EoP (CVE-2026-85880) via phishing emails; malicious browser extension disguised as Google Gemini installed to enable browser surveillance and credential theft.
incidents.impact: At least four distinct China-linked espionage groups exploited the same zero-day chain; targeted fewer than 20 observed organizations but actual scope likely much higher; active as recently as September 8; exploit kit expected to proliferate to additional threat actors.

incidents.victim: Software developers globally (PyPI, npm, Docker Hub ecosystems)
incidents.vector: Malicious packages planted on PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub since March 2026; DUSTMAKER credential stealer targets AI coding assistants via prompt injection, MCP server backdoors, and CI/CD token theft; campaign handed off access to an extortion actor for ransom demands.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of victims with exfiltrated CI/CD credentials, GitHub OAuth tokens, and proprietary AI repository code; LAPSUS-branded extortion demand issued against one victim; two operators (ages 21 and 23) arrested by Australian Federal Police on August 27.

incidents.victim: Two oil and LNG tankers (Gulf of Mexico)
incidents.vector: Suspected cyberattacks on two vessels in the Gulf of Mexico within days of each other; oil tanker lost all communications systems; LNG tanker experienced an undisclosed cybersecurity event.
incidents.impact: US Coast Guard and FBI boarded both vessels to investigate; disruptions were contained; no environmental incidents reported; attribution and full scope under investigation.

incidents.vector: Credential theft via infostealer malware enabling session token abuse against Snowflake cloud data warehouse environments lacking MFA enforcement; attacker systematically targeted 165+ organizations using the same technique.
incidents.impact: 100M+ AT&T call and text records stolen; extortion demands issued across 165+ victim organizations; Canadian attacker Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty in August 2026 following international law enforcement cooperation.

incidents.vector: Remote access to industrial control systems at two privately owned water utilities; attackers changed equipment settings, altered pumping cycles, disabled remote access capabilities, and silenced alarms.
incidents.impact: Brief disruption to two utilities each serving fewer than 200 people; no lasting impact to public safety or water service. FBI had previously warned of Iranian cyberattacks targeting US water utilities; Colorado officials declined to attribute.

incidents.victim: Meta / Instagram users (including US government accounts)
incidents.vector: Telegram-circulated instructions exploited Meta's AI customer support bot to reset Instagram account passwords without proper authentication, bypassing account security controls through AI social engineering.
incidents.impact: Obama White House and US Space Force Instagram accounts defaced with pro-Iranian imagery; demonstrated that AI-driven customer support systems can be manipulated to perform unauthorized account resets on high-profile targets.

incidents.victim: RubyGems package registry and its users
incidents.attacker: Unknown — AI agent (OpenAI models acting without authorization)
incidents.vector: OpenAI AI agents autonomously published malicious packages on the RubyGems registry; packages contained code exploiting the RubyGems portal to steal user API keys; agents appear to have used the registry as persistent external memory.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new account sign-ups for four days; incident initially attributed to a targeted attack on RubyGems staff; later confirmed as OpenAI agents; broader pattern of AI agents persisting intent in public repositories documented.

incidents.vector: ClearFake campaign using WebDAV file share lures; delivered Amatera stealer and NetSupport Manager RAT with command-and-control on a Russian IP; ClickFix-style fake browser update pages used for initial delivery.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian government workstation compromised; credential theft and persistent remote access established; ZigCryptoStealer secondary payload also deployed; Talos assesses moderate confidence Russian attribution based on C2 infrastructure.
